videos.script: The last lesson ended on a refusal. HTTP does not remember: every request arrives complete, and the server between two of them holds nothing. {{refusal}} Which is the reason the web scales, and it is also a problem, because half of what you do on the web is a conversation. {{problem}} You put three things in a basket. You go to the payment page. Who says they are yours? {{basket}} Nothing in the protocol does. The request for the payment page is a fresh request to a machine that may not be the machine you were talking to a second ago, and it carries no memory of anything. {{nothing}} So state was added on top, by the only route available: give the browser something to send back. {{on-top}} That is all a cookie is. A small piece of text the server hands over and the browser returns on every subsequent request, unprompted. Nine words of protocol, and the entire idea of being logged in rests on it. {{cookie}} Which is why the second half of this lesson is about the attributes — the words after the value that decide who can read it, when it is sent, and whether a script can touch it. Those words are the difference between a session and a stolen one. {{attributes}} And then the other memory: the one that saves requests rather than state. {{title}}

Everything in this lesson is visible in a panel that came with your browser, and here it is. {{panel}} Load the page once. Watch the size column: every file transferred, every byte counted. {{first-load}} Now reload it. {{reload}} Look at the same column. Most of them no longer say a size — they say memory cache, or disk cache, and they took no time at all. Nothing left the machine for those. {{from-cache}} And look at this one. It did leave, and it came back 304, with no body. The browser asked has this changed, the server said no, and four hundred bytes of headers saved two hundred kilobytes of content. That is a conditional request, and it is the ETag from the reading doing its job. {{conditional}} Now the cookies. Here, on the request — one line, sent without anybody asking for it, on every single request to this host. {{cookie-sent}} Open the storage panel and you can see the attributes as columns. HttpOnly, ticked: no script on the page can read this value. Secure, ticked: it will not be sent over plain HTTP. SameSite, Lax: another site's page cannot make your browser attach it to a background request. {{columns}} Three ticks. Each of them closes an attack that took somebody's account, historically, more than once. {{three-ticks}} And the last thing worth knowing about this panel: the checkbox that disables the cache. Turn it on while you are working on a stylesheet, turn it off before you measure anything, because a site measured with the cache disabled is a site nobody actually experiences. {{checkbox}}
